svg.title: Sliding Window
svg.desc: Sliding Window. Slide a window along a sequence, adding the item that enters and dropping the one that leaves, instead of re-scanning each window. Step 1, Recount every window: Recount: add up each window of 3 from scratch. 8 windows × 3 = 24 item reads; the best sum is 17. Step 2, Slide: add one, drop one: Slide: add the item that enters, subtract the one that leaves. Same sums and best in 17 reads: O(n). Step 3, Grow and shrink: Variable window: right adds a letter; a repeat makes left jump past its earlier copy. Best: stream. Step 4, Windows in real systems: Rate limit, 5 per 60 s: at 52 s the window is full, so 429; at 61 s the 0 s request has aged out.

g.text: Recount: add up each window of 3 from scratch. 8 windows × 3 = 24 item reads; the best sum is 17.
Slide: add the item that enters, subtract the one that leaves. Same sums and best in 17 reads: O(n).
Variable window: right adds a letter; a repeat makes left jump past its earlier copy. Best: stream.
Rate limit, 5 per 60 s: at 52 s the window is full, so 429; at 61 s the 0 s request has aged out.

g.text: Recount: for each window of 3, add up its items from scratch, then move on to the next window.
Neighbouring windows share 2 items, so most items are read 3 times: the dots inside the cells count the reads.
8 windows × 3 items = 24 reads for 10 items. Cost O(n·k): each item is read up to k times.
Slide: add up the first window once, then each move adds the item that enters and subtracts the one that leaves.
Each item is read at most twice: ● when it enters the window and ● when it leaves.
Same sums, same best (17), in 3 + 7 × 2 = 17 reads instead of 24.
A million items with k = 1,000: about 2 million reads instead of about a billion. O(n), whatever k is.
last seen: letter → index (a hash map)

g.text: ■ in the window□ a repeat■ left behind
right adds one letter at a time. A letter already inside the window makes left jump just past its earlier copy.
a at 3 repeats a at 1 → left = 2
t at 5 repeats t at 2 → left = 3
a at 8 repeats a at 3 → left = 4
Longest: stream (indexes 4–9), length 6. Each index enters once and leaves at most once: O(n).
● accepted● refused (429)○ aged out: older than 60 s▬ the window: the last 60 s

g.text: Each request: drop times older than 60 s from the front, count the rest, and accept (and log) it if there are fewer than 5.
TCP flow control: the receive window
Memory: at most 5 timestamps per client. Each time is appended once and dropped once, so a request costs O(1) amortized.
